language_mix: No language-ID library is installed (no fasttext or langdetect), so I used a heuristic on text with chrome and LaTeX removed. It computes English, Spanish and French stopword ratios (fixed lists of about 100, 90 and 40 words) and the ASCII share of letters. A doc is 'en' if en_ratio >= max(es, fr) and en_ratio >= 0.15; 'es' or 'fr' if that ratio beats English and is >= 0.15; 'non_latin' if ASCII letters < 0.5; docs under 20 letter-tokens are 'too_short'. Results: en 55,437 (89.0%, 500.9M chars); too_short 4,681 (7.5%, mostly chrome or TOC stubs); es 1,457 (2.34% of docs, 10.45M chars, 2.0%); unclear_low_stopword 654 (tables, chronologies, exercise lists); fr 24 (some are mislabeled chronologies); non_latin 16 (Arabic-course pages). Spanish docs by host: espanol 913, human 377 (Spanish-language courses), math 166 (the Santiago Canyon 'HiSet Mathematica' course), chem 1. Some espanol content looks machine-translated: TOC text such as 'Resumen de Key Concepts' and LaTeX whose commands were translated and spaced, e.g. '\ (\ begin {array} {ras a la izquierda}'. The filter dropped 995 of the 998 espanol-host docs, and only 4 docs my heuristic marks non-English survived it.

issues.name: Within-source near-duplicates (the same OpenStax/Lumen chapters copied into many Courses remixes)
issues.description: LibreTexts 'Courses' are remixes of 'Bookshelves' books, so the same section appears many times with small edits. Template stub pages also cluster, e.g. 98 Lumen 'Self Check' pages that contain only quiz instructions and no quiz.
issues.prevalence: MinHash ran on chrome-stripped text of docs with >=30 words: 57,551 docs. Results: 16,818 verified pairs (estimated Jaccard >=0.8), 7,486 clusters with 21,086 docs (33.9% of all docs). Keeping one copy per cluster removes 13,600 docs and 146,614,233 raw chars (28.0% of all chars). 7,841 of the verified pairs (46.6%) link a Courses page to a Bookshelves page. Exact duplicates on normalized raw text: 3,772 docs in groups, 2,110 extra copies. On normalized chrome-stripped text (>=200 chars): 4,423 docs, 2,484 extra copies, 23.8M chars.
issues.measurement_method: Word 5-shingles of re.findall(r'\w+', clean.lower()), each hashed with xxh64. 128 multiply-shift permutations ((a*h+b)>>32, seed 0) give the signature; LSH uses 16 bands x 8 rows. A candidate pair is kept if the fraction of equal signature slots is >=0.8. Clusters are built with union-find. Spot check of exact shingle Jaccard on raw text: 0.948 for a Widener 5.02 / OpenStax Atoms First 8.2 pair, and 0.74 for two Lumen Self Check stubs. Exact dups: md5 of lowercased, whitespace-collapsed text.

The largest cluster is 98 Lumen 'Self Check' quiz stubs; the next largest are OpenStax Chemistry sections copied into 18 to 22 course remixes.
filtered_comparison:
Docs were matched by id. All 40,049 filtered ids exist in raw. Raw docs: 22,182 dropped (35.6%), 8,443 changed (13.6% of raw, 21.1% of kept), 31,644 unchanged.

What was dropped:
(a) Every raw doc under 700 chars: 7,360 of 7,360. The shortest kept raw doc is 700 chars.
(b) Spanish: 995 of the 998 espanol-host docs.
(c) Chrome-only pages: 995 of 1,051 site-chrome docs and 3,223 of 3,531 single-line TOC pages.
(d) Many near-duplicates. Docs in my near-dup clusters were dropped at 58% (11,832 of 20,404, counting docs >=500 chars and not already explained by a), b) or c)). Other docs were dropped at 6.8% (2,278 of 33,393).
Sequential attribution of drops: <500 chars 5,145; non-English 1,460; site chrome 995; no content after chrome 472; in a near-dup cluster 11,832; unexplained 2,278. The dataset cards do not document the filter steps, so the link to dedup is an association I measured, not a confirmed mechanism.

What still survives in the filtered version:
- 1,467 near-dup clusters still have 2 or more kept copies, which is 1,624 extra docs and 15.0M chars; 538 clusters were dropped completely.
- Chrome was not stripped from kept docs: 'Last updated...Save as PDF' in 8,452 docs (21.1%), lone '-' lines in 16,810 (42.0%), \PageIndex in 7,697 (19.2%), 'selected template' in 1,503, 'Skip to main content' in 1,097, 302 inline TOC pages, and 39 MindTouch blobs.
- 7 docs are empty and 11 are under 200 chars.

How the 8,443 changed docs differ:
(1) Spans deleted with no replacement in 7,146 docs, 2,257,215 chars in total. These look like sentence-level deletions that leave double spaces or dangling numbers. Many of the deleted sentences are benign: an optics exercise 'You are told not to shoot until you see the whites of their eyes.', 'Suppose the amount of mass in a black hole doubles.', blood-pressure exercise text, a child-maltreatment learning objective. The cause is not documented.
(2) PII placeholders in 1,745 docs: filtered has 1,275 <EMAIL_ADDRESS>, 1,573 <IP_ADDRESS> and 418 <PHONE_NUMBER>. The replacement also removes the space before it. Of 3,021 replacements I aligned to raw text, 2,218 (73.4%) are evident false positives: section numbers such as 'Sections: 2.2.1.2.8' becoming '<IP_ADDRESS>.8' (743); DOIs and other dotted numbers (458); URLs and image filenames such as 'muso-soseki-3.@2x.jpeg' or a cnx.org URL (715 + 61); page ranges, numbers in tables and LaTeX numbers as phone numbers (241). 803 are plausible real values, e.g. faculty emails and phone numbers. 7 docs were emptied.
license_notes: Metadata license counts (all 62,269 docs): CC BY 4.0: 39,339. CC BY-SA 4.0: 18,065. Public Domain: 1,593. CC BY 3.0: 1,292. CC BY-SA 3.0: 1,010. GNU FDL: 967. CC BY-SA 2.5: 3. No doc lacks a license value. Docs dropped by the filter, by license: CC BY 15,337 of 40,631; CC BY-SA 6,234 of 19,078; Public Domain 401 of 1,593; GFDL 210 of 967. The license values are per-page tags, but 2,036 docs (3.27%) say in the body that some content is NC, ND, all-rights-reserved or used-with-permission. The metadata license does not cover that content.

recommended_steps.step: Drop pages that are only chrome: docs that start with 'Skip to main content' and contain the MindTouch breadcrumb block, single-line docs that match INLINE_HEADER, and any doc with fewer than 200 chars of content after chrome removal and title stripping.
recommended_steps.rationale: These docs have no article text. They teach UI strings, JSON blobs and TOC lists.
recommended_steps.evidence: 1,051 site-chrome docs (7.66M chars, 1.46%), 3,515 inline-header TOC pages and 4,926 docs (7.91%) with less than 200 content chars. 39 MindTouch docs and 302 TOC pages are still in the filtered version.

recommended_steps.step: Strip chrome lines inside the remaining docs: the 'Last updated'/'Save as PDF'/'Page ID' header lines and the following byline bullets, 'selected template will load here'/'This action is not available.', lone '-' lines, and runs of 3 or more 'N.M: Title' TOC lines. Use the strip_chrome() function in analyze.py, which has a --selftest.
recommended_steps.rationale: This chrome sits at the start of 30 to 41% of docs and repeats in the same form across the corpus.
recommended_steps.evidence: Header lines in 18,912 docs (30.4%), lone '-' lines in 25,730 docs (41.3%), bylines in 7,485 docs. Filtered still has 'Last updated...Save as PDF' in 21.1% of docs and lone dashes in 42.0%.

recommended_steps.step: After chrome stripping, run MinHash near-dedup within the source (word 5-shingles, Jaccard >= 0.8, keep one per cluster). Keep the Bookshelves copy, or the longest copy if there is no Bookshelves copy. Dedup this source with the other OER sources too, because OpenStax books recur elsewhere.
recommended_steps.rationale: Courses remixes copy Bookshelves books almost verbatim, so the duplicates would over-weight a few OpenStax and Lumen books.
recommended_steps.evidence: 13,600 extra copies, 146.6M chars (28.0% of raw). 46.6% of verified pairs are Courses<->Bookshelves. Filtered still has 1,624 extra docs (15.0M chars) in 1,467 clusters.

recommended_steps.step: Normalize the LaTeX instead of removing it: replace \(\PageIndex{X}\) with X, and delete \nonumber, \label{...}, \\[Npt] and \hspace/\vspace{...}. Keep \( \) and \[ \] math. Drop docs with spaced or translated LaTeX ('\ dfrac {', '\ (\ begin'), or repair the common commands. Remove unresolved '( [label] )' and '[link]' references.
recommended_steps.rationale: Math is a large, valuable share of the corpus. The leftover macros and broken commands teach syntax that cannot render.
recommended_steps.evidence: Math spans are 6.71% of chars in 33.8% of docs. \PageIndex is in 13,521 docs (2.23M chars). Layout residue is in 6,953 docs (1.00M chars). Spaced LaTeX is in 497 docs; crossref residue in 110.

recommended_steps.step: Run a real language-ID model (fastText lid.176) and either drop non-English docs or route them to a separate Spanish pool, with extra caution for espanol-host pages that look machine-translated.
recommended_steps.rationale: The source is meant to be English. My stopword heuristic finds Spanish outside the espanol host as well.
recommended_steps.evidence: 1,457 'es' docs (10.45M chars): espanol 913, human 377, math 166. Translated LaTeX example: '\ (\ begin {array} {ras a la izquierda}'.

recommended_steps.step: Do not use the Common Pile filtered text as-is. Start from raw and apply your own filters. If PII redaction is needed, use rules that skip URLs, DOIs, dotted section numbers, image filenames and numeric tables, and keep the surrounding whitespace.
recommended_steps.rationale: The existing pipeline deleted benign sentences, which leaves broken exercises, and its PII step mostly redacts non-PII. It also did not remove the chrome.
recommended_steps.evidence: 7,146 docs had span deletions (2.26M chars), e.g. '102. You are told not to shoot until you see the whites of their eyes. If the eyes...' became '102.  If the eyes...'. 2,218 of 3,021 PII replacements (73.4%) are evident false positives. 7 docs were emptied.

recommended_steps.step: Repair inline-element damage: delete the space before , ; : . when it follows a letter, rejoin short split-line fragments with their neighbors, and join flattened ordinals ('19 th' to '19th'). As an option, rejoin flattened chemical formulas on chem and bio pages ('H 2 O' to 'H2O', '[Cu(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+' to '[Cu(H2O)6]2+'), or flag those docs.
recommended_steps.rationale: These are systematic HTML-to-text faults that make the text less natural and spell formulas wrong.
recommended_steps.evidence: Space before punctuation in 33,463 docs (53.7%). Split fragments in 3,850 docs. Flattened chemical or orbital notation in 3,751 docs. Split ordinals in 934 docs.

recommended_steps.step: Strip 'Contributors and Attributions' footers, 'Authored by/License/Located at' lines, '↵' reference and footnote lines, and URLs whose display text was truncated with '...'.
recommended_steps.rationale: Boilerplate and broken URLs that repeat across thousands of pages.
recommended_steps.evidence: Attribution: 8,039 docs, 2.78M chars. '↵' lines: 1,877 docs, 1.88M chars. Truncated URLs: 3,585 docs, 0.69M chars.

recommended_steps.step: Review license conflicts: drop docs, or strip the text segments, whose body says the adapted text is CC BY-NC(-SA), ND, all rights reserved or used with permission. Mentions that refer only to embedded media that was not extracted (YouTube, images) can be kept once the attribution line is stripped.
recommended_steps.rationale: Some page-level CC BY tags cover text adapted from NC-licensed sources.
recommended_steps.evidence: 2,036 docs (3.27%), e.g. text 'Lifespan Development ... by Martha Lally and Suzanne Valentine-French is licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0' under metadata 'Creative Commons - Attribution'.

recommended_steps.step: After cleaning, drop stub pages: quiz or self-check pages without questions, calculator or applet pages, and video-only pages. Then apply a minimum-content filter on the cleaned text (for example >=50 words of prose) instead of on raw length.
recommended_steps.rationale: Raw length counts the chrome, so a raw-length threshold removes short real pages and keeps chrome-heavy ones.
recommended_steps.evidence: A cluster of 98 Lumen 'Self Check' stubs. 1,484 docs with interactive placeholders. The filter used a raw cut of >=700 chars, yet 340 kept docs have less than 200 content chars.

open_questions: The dataset cards do not document the steps that produced libretexts_filtered. The strong link between drops and my near-dup clusters (58% vs 6.8% drop rate), and the sentence-level deletions, are measured associations. The exact filters (dedup method, sentence-level toxicity or quality classifier) should be checked in the r-three/common-pile GitHub code.
Both READMEs give sizes 10x larger than the measured text: 5.3 GB vs 0.523 G chars for raw, and 3.6 GB vs 0.359 G chars for filtered. The cause is unknown.
Language labels come from a stopword heuristic because no language-ID library is installed. The 'fr' label (24 docs) includes chronologies, so a real LID model should confirm the non-English counts.

The chrome rules may remove a little real content: a 1 to 3 line '- ' bullet list right after 'Save as PDF' that is shorter than 100 chars would be counted as a byline. I did not measure that error rate.
The inline-footnote-number regex is low precision (its top examples fall inside site chrome), so its count of 3,769 docs is an upper bound.
The PII false-positive classes come from context heuristics. The 'plausible' class (803) was not checked by hand and may also contain section numbers or numbers inside URLs.
